newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan allows hog breeding to resume after epidemic.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan allows hog breeding to resume after epidemic.

text.p: Taiwan's Council of Agriculture said on Tuesday pig farms shut down following the island's recent foot and month epidemic could apply to resume breeding.
"Pig farmers can apply to re-start their breeding under our guidelines," a council official said. "But we do not expect any pork exports to resume."
Taiwan on March 20 banned pork exports and ordered a mass slaughter and inoculation drive after an outbreak of the highly contagious foot and mouth disease was confirmed.
The council official said farmers may resume breeding only in farms that have not seen any outbreak of the disease for at least one month.
He added farmers were required to vaccinate new-born pigs.
Taiwan lifted the export ban on April 17, but none of its major pork markets, including Japan, has agreed to resume importing Taiwan pork.
